title: Crown and Veil
premise: Quentin Sterling, a cartographer who maps realms that shouldn't exist, has spent years hiding among the ledgers of the Guild of Impossible Things, trading in memories, names, and small mercies. When a mute child arrives speaking a language older than any kingdom, Quentin recognizes it as the tongue of the court beneath the mountain—and realizes the child is a soul sold there by her own guild decades ago. To free her, Quentin must descend into the Undercourt and bargain with its veiled sovereign, discovering along the way that she herself was once sold too, and that her memories of love were the price of her survival. In the end, Quentin trades her own name and every map she's ever drawn to buy both souls back, choosing to become unmapped rather than let the child pay for her survival.
about_author: Marguerite Voss is the pen name of a former archivist who spent eleven years cataloguing estate sales before turning to fiction. She writes from a drafty attic full of unlabeled maps and insists none of them are hers.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Quentin Sterling catalogs an ordinary week of impossible trades at the Guild—bottled grief, a borrowed shadow—establishing her careful invisibility. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: weary contentment masking old fear.

chapters.title: A Knock in Dead Tongues
chapters.summary: On the winter solstice, a child of about seven appears at the guild door, speaking a language no living scholar knows. Quentin alone can half-understand her. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: dread awakening like an old scar reopening.

chapters.title: What the Guild Sells
chapters.summary: Quentin searches the forbidden back-ledgers and finds a transaction from forty years past: a soul sold to the court beneath the mountain. The seller's signature is her own handwriting. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: vertigo of self-betrayal.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Oath
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: young Quentin apprenticed to the guild, learning that maps are contracts and blank spaces are debts. She swears never to map the Undercourt. POV: Quentin (past). Emotional beat: ambition curdling into caution.

chapters.title: The Child Who Remembers Forward
chapters.summary: The child, whom Quentin names Wren, draws pictures of events that haven't happened—including Quentin's death beneath the mountain. POV: alternating Quentin/Wren. Emotional beat: tenderness tangled with terror.

chapters.title: Guildmasters and Grave Prices
chapters.summary: Quentin petitions the Guildmaster for sanctioned rescue; he refuses, revealing that rescinding a soul-sale requires payment of equal weight. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: betrayal by institution.

chapters.title: Stolen Ink
chapters.summary: Quentin steals the guild's master key—a vial of ink distilled from a first memory—and prepares to forge her own passage-map to the Undercourt. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: resolve hardening into transgression.

chapters.title: The Road That Unwrites Itself
chapters.summary: Quentin and Wren travel toward the mountain; the road erases landmarks behind them, punishing cartographers. They shelter with a ferryman who owes Quentin a debt. POV: Quentin. Emotional bond deepens; beat: found-family warmth against encroaching dread.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Toll
chapters.summary: The ferryman demands a memory as toll; Quentin pays one and cannot afterward recall why she flinches at lullabies. First hint her past holds love. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: grief without object.

chapters.title: Beneath the Mountain's Skin
chapters.summary: They enter the Undercourt through a door made of unspoken words. The realm runs on traded names; strangers must surrender theirs at the gate. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: eerie wonder, the child oddly at home.

chapters.title: Court of Veils
chapters.summary: Quentin bargains before the veiled Sovereign, who wears the faces of everyone who ever sold something there. The price for Wren's soul: a soul of equal weight. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: cold negotiation over burning panic.

chapters.title: The Weight of a Soul
chapters.summary: Quentin offers her own soul; the scales refuse—it is already partially owned. Someone bought pieces of her long ago. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: horror of discovering oneself as merchandise.

chapters.title: Ledger of the Sold
chapters.summary: Quentin infiltrates the Undercourt archives and finds her own entry: at nineteen, she sold her memories of a lover named Ilse to survive a plague-winter. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: mourning someone she cannot remember loving.

chapters.title: Ilse
chapters.summary: In the Court's memory-vaults, Quentin experiences the returned fragments: Ilse's laugh, a shared map-drawn future, the choice to forget so she could live. POV: interleaved past/present. Emotional beat: devastating reawakening of love.

chapters.title: The Sovereign's Face
chapters.summary: Quentin lifts the Sovereign's veil and finds Ilse—or what became of her after selling her own heart to buy Quentin's survival. The lovers' trades are entangled. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: recognition and ruin.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Ilse-as-Sovereign offers a cruel mercy: Wren goes free if Quentin stays as the Court's new cartographer forever. Wren refuses to leave without her. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: love against duty at full tension.

chapters.title: Wren's Bargain
chapters.summary: Wren reveals she came to the surface deliberately: she is the Court's future, sent to fetch a cartographer willing to redraw its dying borders. Her prophecy-pictures were warnings, not threats. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: innocence revealed as agency.

chapters.title: Redrawing the Borders
chapters.summary: Quentin proposes a third path: instead of paying souls, she will remap the Undercourt, giving it new borders so it no longer needs to consume them. Ilse warns the mapping will cost Quentin everything she is. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: defiant hope.

chapters.title: The Map of Everything She Is
chapters.summary: Climax begins: Quentin draws the new map using her stolen ink, feeding in her memories, her name, her craft, line by line, as the Court reshapes around her art. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: self-annihilation as creation.

chapters.title: Unmapped
chapters.summary: Climax resolves: the map completes; the Undercourt stabilizes; Ilse is freed from the veil but remembers only fragments of Quentin, who now exists on no ledger anywhere. Wren leads the nameless Quentin home. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: triumph hollowed by loss.

chapters.title: The Language Predating Kingdoms
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Wren teaches surface children the old tongue while Quentin, unnamed but not empty, begins drawing again—for pleasure, not contract. Ilse arrives at the guild door holding a map she doesn't remember making: of two women and a garden. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: fragile rebirth.

chapters.title: Crown and Veil
chapters.summary: Quentin chooses not to reclaim her traded memories, understanding some prices should stay paid—but she and Ilse begin again anyway, courting as strangers. The final image: a new ledger opened, first line blank, waiting. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: quiet, earned hope.
